lessons.title: Time and the calendar
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB National Syllabus, Mathematics, Level III (Classes 5-6) — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Read the time on a clock and use the 12-hour and 24-hour systems.
Calculate durations, start times and finishing times.
Use the calendar: days, weeks, months, years and leap years.
reviewNotes: Leap-year rule: only 'every 4 years' is taught; the exception for century years (1900, 2100) is not covered at this level.
12-hour/24-hour clock: check which one the FSLC paper uses.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Units of time
blocks.md: 60 seconds = 1 minute; 60 minutes = 1 hour; 24 hours = 1 day; 7 days = 1 week; 12 months = 1 year; 365 days = 1 year, and 366 days in a **leap year** (every 4 years, for example 2024 and 2028). **30 days** have April, June, September and November. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year). The other months have 31.

blocks.caption: A clock showing 3:45.
blocks.alt: A clock face. The short hour hand points between 3 and 4. The long minute hand points to 9. The clock shows quarter to four.

blocks.title: 12-hour and 24-hour clock
blocks.md: The 24-hour clock counts from 00:00 to 23:59. From 13:00 onwards subtract 12 to get the pm time: 15:45 is 3:45 pm. Add 12 to a pm time to get the 24-hour time: 8:30 pm is 20:30. Midnight is 00:00 and midday is 12:00.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Working with 100 minutes in an hour: there are only **60**. 2 h 45 min + 30 min = 3 h 15 min, not 2 h 75 min.
- Forgetting that some months have 30 days and others 31.
- Counting the first day twice when you find the number of days between two dates.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A bus leaves at 08:45 and the journey lasts 3 hours 50 minutes. At what time does it arrive?
steps: Add the minutes: 11:45 + 50 min = 11:95, which is 12:35 (95 − 60 = 35 and one more hour).

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: How many days are there from 12 March to 5 April in a year that is not a leap year?
steps: From 31 March to 5 April: 5 more days.

lessons.title: Converting units of length, mass, capacity and time
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB National Syllabus, Mathematics, Level III (Classes 5-6) — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Convert between units of length, mass, capacity and time.
Add and subtract measures with mixed units.
Solve problems that need a change of units.
reviewNotes: The existing 'Measurement' lesson also covers basic conversions; this lesson adds mixed-unit sums and problems.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Units to remember
blocks.md:
- Length: 1 km = 1,000 m; 1 m = 100 cm; 1 cm = 10 mm.
- Mass: 1 kg = 1,000 g; 1 tonne = 1,000 kg.
- Capacity: 1 litre = 1,000 ml (millilitres).
- Time: 1 h = 60 min; 1 min = 60 s.
To go from a **big** unit to a **small** one, multiply. To go from small to big, divide.

items.text: Big unit to small unit: multiply. Small to big: divide.

blocks.caption: How to change between kilometres, metres, centimetres and millimetres.
blocks.alt: Four boxes in a row: km, m, cm and mm. Arrows going right say times 1,000, times 100 and times 10. Arrows going left say divide by the same numbers.

blocks.title: Mixed units
blocks.md: To add or subtract, change everything to the **same small unit** first. Example: 2 kg 700 g + 1 kg 450 g = 2,700 g + 1,450 g = 4,150 g = 4 kg 150 g. For time, do not use 100: 1 h 45 min = 105 minutes.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Multiplying when you should divide (km to m: multiply; g to kg: divide).
- Adding numbers with **different units** (like 2 m + 50 cm = 52!). Change first: 2 m + 50 cm = 250 cm.
- Using 100 for time: there are 60 minutes in an hour.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Change 3.5 km to metres, and 2,750 g to kilograms.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A tailor has a roll of cloth 5 m long. He cuts 3 m 40 cm. How much cloth is left?
steps: Change to centimetres: 5 m = 500 cm and 3 m 40 cm = 340 cm.

lessons.title: Speed, distance and time
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB National Syllabus, Mathematics, Level III (Classes 5-6) — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Calculate speed, distance or time from the other two.
Change minutes to hours in speed problems.
Find an average speed for a whole journey.
reviewNotes: Average speed uses 'total distance ÷ total time'; check this is expected at Class 6.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: The speed rule
blocks.md: **Speed = distance ÷ time.** If a car travels 180 km in 3 hours, its speed is 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h (kilometres per hour). From this we get: **distance = speed × time** and **time = distance ÷ speed**. The units must agree: km with hours gives km/h; metres with seconds gives m/s.

items.text: D = S × T    S = D ÷ T    T = D ÷ S
D: distance   S: speed   T: time

blocks.caption: The speed triangle: cover the one you want.
blocks.alt: A box split into three parts: D on the top, S at bottom left and T at bottom right. Below are the three formulas for D, S and T.

blocks.title: Minutes and hours
blocks.md: Change minutes to hours **before** you use km/h: 30 min = 0.5 h; 45 min = 0.75 h; 15 min = 0.25 h; 20 min = 1/3 h. Example: at 60 km/h for 45 minutes, the distance is 60 × 0.75 = 45 km.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Using minutes with km/h without changing to hours.
- Finding an **average speed** by adding two speeds and dividing by 2. The correct way: **total distance ÷ total time**.
- Dividing the wrong way: time is distance ÷ speed, not speed ÷ distance.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A bus travels 150 km at 50 km/h. How long does the journey take?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A man goes 100 km at 50 km/h, then another 100 km at 100 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
steps: Time for the first part: 100 ÷ 50 = 2 h. Second part: 100 ÷ 100 = 1 h.
Total distance 200 km; total time 3 h.
